description: Extend the error taxonomy with payment-specific error classes and update the error handler tests. Adds five new ErrorCodes entries, five corresponding AppError subclasses, ERROR_CATALOG entries for each, and tests in the error-handler test suite covering each new class plus the full envelope shape. FEAT-002 depends on the classes defined here.
steps: 1. In src/utils/errors.ts, add five new entries to the ErrorCodes const object (after the existing entries): INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS: 'INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS', INVALID_CURRENCY: 'INVALID_CURRENCY', PAYMENT_DECLINED: 'PAYMENT_DECLINED', DUPLICATE_PAYMENT: 'DUPLICATE_PAYMENT', PAYMENT_NOT_FOUND: 'PAYMENT_NOT_FOUND'.

2. In src/utils/errors.ts, add corresponding entries to ERROR_CATALOG immediately after the SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE entry: INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS → { statusCode: 422, code: 'INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS', message: 'Insufficient funds to complete the payment', expose: true }, INVALID_CURRENCY → { statusCode: 422, code: 'INVALID_CURRENCY', message: 'The specified currency is not supported', expose: true }, PAYMENT_DECLINED → { statusCode: 422, code: 'PAYMENT_DECLINED', message: 'The payment was declined', expose: true }, DUPLICATE_PAYMENT → { statusCode: 409, code: 'DUPLICATE_PAYMENT', message: 'A payment with this reference already exists', expose: true }, PAYMENT_NOT_FOUND → { statusCode: 404, code: 'PAYMENT_NOT_FOUND', message: 'The requested payment was not found', expose: true }.

3. In src/utils/errors.ts, add five error classes after ServiceUnavailableError, following the exact pattern of existing classes (extend AppError, set this.name, use Object.setPrototypeOf via new.target.prototype in the AppError constructor): class InsufficientFundsError extends AppError { constructor(message = 'Insufficient funds to complete the payment', details?: ErrorDetails) { super(422, ErrorCodes.INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS, message, { details }); this.name = 'InsufficientFundsError'; } }; class InvalidCurrencyError extends AppError { constructor(currency: string, details?: ErrorDetails) { super(422, ErrorCodes.INVALID_CURRENCY, `Currency '${currency}' is not supported`, { details }); this.name = 'InvalidCurrencyError'; } }; class PaymentDeclinedError extends AppError { constructor(message = 'The payment was declined', details?: ErrorDetails) { super(422, ErrorCodes.PAYMENT_DECLINED, message, { details }); this.name = 'PaymentDeclinedError'; } }; class DuplicatePaymentError extends AppError { constructor(message = 'A payment with this reference already exists', details?: ErrorDetails) { super(409, ErrorCodes.DUPLICATE_PAYMENT, message, { details }); this.name = 'DuplicatePaymentError'; } }; class PaymentNotFoundError extends AppError { constructor(message = 'The requested payment was not found', details?: ErrorDetails) { super(404, ErrorCodes.PAYMENT_NOT_FOUND, message, { details }); this.name = 'PaymentNotFoundError'; } }.

4. Export all five new classes from src/utils/errors.ts (add them to the existing export list at the bottom if there is one, or they are automatically exported by class declaration since the file has no barrel-style re-export — the classes are declared at module scope so they are already exported).

5. In src/middleware/__tests__/error-handler.test.ts: (a) Import the five new error classes from ../../utils/errors. (b) In the buildApp() function, add five new routes that throw one new error class each: GET /payment-insufficient-funds → throws new InsufficientFundsError(); GET /payment-invalid-currency → throws new InvalidCurrencyError('XYZ'); GET /payment-declined → throws new PaymentDeclinedError(); GET /payment-duplicate → throws new DuplicatePaymentError('Duplicate tip', { idempotencyKey: 'key-1' }); GET /payment-not-found → throws new PaymentNotFoundError(). (c) In the 'maps status codes to the correct HTTP response' test, add these cases to the cases array: ['/payment-insufficient-funds', 422, 'INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS'], ['/payment-invalid-currency', 422, 'INVALID_CURRENCY'], ['/payment-declined', 422, 'PAYMENT_DECLINED'], ['/payment-duplicate', 409, 'DUPLICATE_PAYMENT'], ['/payment-not-found', 404, 'PAYMENT_NOT_FOUND']. (d) Add a dedicated describe block 'payment-specific error classes' with individual tests: one test per class that verifies the HTTP status code, the code field, a truthy message, and that details are included when passed (DuplicatePaymentError test should check body.error.details.idempotencyKey === 'key-1'). (e) Add a test 'payment errors never leak internal details' that hits /payment-declined and asserts the response JSON does not contain any database/stack artifact strings.
acceptance_criteria: All five new ErrorCode values exist in the ErrorCodes const and in ERROR_CATALOG with the correct statusCode.
All five error classes are exported from src/utils/errors.ts and are instanceof AppError.

Each class sets this.name to the class name and has the correct statusCode: InsufficientFundsError and InvalidCurrencyError and PaymentDeclinedError → 422, DuplicatePaymentError → 409, PaymentNotFoundError → 404.
normalizeError() routes all five new classes through the isAppError branch (no changes to error-handler.ts needed for this), returning the correct statusCode and code.
Running `pnpm test -- src/middleware/__tests__/error-handler.test.ts` passes all existing tests and all new payment error tests.
findings: All 23 tests pass (13 existing + 6 new payment-specific + 4 existing normalizeError/buildErrorResponse). No TS errors in changed files. Pre-existing TS errors exist in other project files (src/config/schema.ts, src/domains/*, etc.) but are unrelated to FEAT-001. The npx tsc --noEmit command exits non-zero due to those pre-existing errors.
